issues.passage: The once unattainable target was finished before lunch on the team's first quiet day.
issues.why: "Once unattainable" is natural, correct English: it means the target used to be out of reach and later became achievable. Finishing it after it ceased to be unattainable does not misuse the word.

fix.correctPassage: For many applicants, admission to the program remains unattainable without substantial financial aid.
wrongPassages: The unattainable target was finished before lunch on the team's first quiet day.
Hikers called the ridge unattainable only after the new trail delivered them to the summit.
She treated the unattainable deadline as generous, since the report had already been submitted.

issues.passage: Officials moved to sanction the misconduct by promoting those responsible and expanding their budget.
issues.why: Sanction also means official permission/approval. Promoting the responsible parties and expanding their budget is a natural reading of officially endorsing the misconduct, so the sentence is valid under the listed definition.

fix.correctPassage: The league may sanction the franchise for repeated violations of recruitment rules.
wrongPassages: Officials insisted they had sanctioned the misconduct simply by hoping the story would fade from the news.
She claimed she could sanction the treaty simply by forgetting to schedule any formal review.
The committee hoped to sanction the reform by refusing to put it on the agenda at all.
